newsitem.title: USA: Sands Regent says defaults on loan.
newsitem.headline: Sands Regent says defaults on loan.

text.p: Sands Regent Inc said falling revenues and profits at its flaghip hotel and casino here, The Sands Regency, have put it in default on its long-term debt agreement.
The debt amounted to $11.0 million at March 31, the company said in a statement issued late on Friday.
Sands Regent said it is currently in discussions with the lender. Further details were undisclosed.
Sands Regent reported a loss of $0.08 a share on revenue of $13.2 million in its third quarter ended March 31 versus a profit of $0.12 a share on revenue of $15.3 million last year.
"The Sands Regency, and many of our competitors, continue to experience depressed revenues as a result of the sluggish Reno tourism market," said Pete Cladianos, president.
The flagship hotel also has been affected by newly expanded gambling operations in Reno and competition from Las Vegas and Native American casinos in the Pacific Northwest.
Sands Regent said losses in Reno were "somewhat offset" by profits at its Copa Casino in Gulfport, Mississippi.
Separately, the company said a trial date in October 1997 has been set for its litigation with two Mississippi regulatory agencies.
